title: Importing routines from a Hevy link copies Hevy's pages through a hidden browser without Hevy's permission
what: A member pastes a Hevy share link and the app opens Hevy's web page out of sight, listens in on the data Hevy's page loads for itself, and copies the routines out of it. The link is often someone else's shared folder. Hevy's terms say nothing from their app may be copied or reused without written permission, and Hevy offers an official way in that needs their approval. Hevy could block it at any time or complain to us or to Google Play.
expected: Routines come in only from the member's own export file, or through Hevy's official way in with Hevy's approval, or the owner decides in writing that he accepts this risk.
fix_line: Owner decides: ask Hevy for approval, switch to their official way in, or drop the link import and keep the file import

title: Google Play asks for the app's top and bottom bar colours to be updated for Android 15, and the app has not done it
what: Play Console shows a recommended action on the live version: the app still uses old ways of colouring the phone's top and bottom bars that Android 15 has retired. The app frame sets the top bar style on every start. On newer phones the bars may look wrong, and Google may turn this into a requirement.
expected: The app draws behind the bars in the way Android 15 expects, and the Play Console recommendation is gone.
fix_line: Move the bar colouring to the Android 15 way and check the Play recommendation clears

title: Google Play wants MettleUp's EU trader status declared by 1 February 2027
what: The Play Console dashboard shows a banner asking the account to declare whether it is a trader in the EU by 1 February 2027. If it is not done, Google may stop showing the app to people in the EU.
expected: The owner fills in the trader declaration in Play Console before the date.
who: the owner; members in the EU
fix_line: Owner declares trader status in Play Console
